dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Log a warning in record_completion_verdict when completion_sidecar.emit returns False (not only when it raises), matching the close gate's dropped-sidecar handling.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py:218-227 wraps emit in try/except and calls logger.warning only in the `except` branch; a non-raising `False` return sets sidecar_written=False with no log

dropped.finding: When completion_sidecar.emit returns False WITHOUT raising (e.g. a LockTimeout that outlasted the single retry), record_completion_verdict records sidecar_written=False but emits no warning — its try/except only logs on a raised exception. The close gate's _emit_completion_sidecar writes an explicit 'Warning: ... WITHOUT ...' stderr line for exactly this dropped-sidecar case; the standalone recorder surfaces the drop only through the returned record field.
scenarios: A standalone verify-completion loses its sidecar to persistent write-lock contention; via CLI the drop is surfaced by _render_record_line's 'sidecar NOT recorded', but a non-CLI/library caller that ignores the record field gets no signal.
